stem: Although the hike was long and steep, the children remained ______ and kept singing all the way to the top.
explanation: The clue is "kept singing" together with "although", which sets their mood against the hard climb: they stayed CHEERFUL. EXHAUSTED is what the long, steep hike would lead you to expect, which is exactly what "although" rules out; SILENT contradicts the singing.

stem: Bilal is so ______ that he arrives at least ten minutes early for every class.
explanation: Arriving early for every class is the definition given in the sentence, so Bilal is PUNCTUAL. CARELESS, FORGETFUL and LAZY all describe someone who would more likely be late.

stem: The new bridge was meant to ______ traffic in the city centre, but it has actually ______ the congestion, with queues now longer than before.
explanation: "But" and "actually" signal that the result went against the plan, and "queues now longer" shows the congestion WORSENED, so the plan was to EASE traffic. "Ease ... reduced" has no contrast and contradicts the longer queues; no one builds a bridge to increase traffic.

stem: The scientist's claims were met with ______ because she had not published any data to support them.
explanation: The cause is given: no data to support the claims, so people doubted them, i.e. SCEPTICISM. ADMIRATION, GRATITUDE and ENTHUSIASM are positive reactions that unsupported claims would not earn.

stem: Fatima's handwriting is so ______ that even her teacher cannot read her notes.
explanation: "Cannot read her notes" defines the blank: ILLEGIBLE means impossible to read. LEGIBLE is the trap; it means easy to read, the exact opposite.

stem: Far from being ______, the report was packed with long, rambling sections that repeated the same points.
explanation: "Far from being" means the report was the opposite of the blank, and it was long and rambling, so the blank is CONCISE (short and clear). VERBOSE, LENGTHY and REPETITIVE all describe what the report actually was, not its opposite.

stem: Once dismissed as ______, the theory has since been ______ by a series of careful experiments, and it is now taught in every textbook.
explanation: "Dismissed" needs a negative first word (FAR-FETCHED), and "now taught in every textbook" shows the experiments proved it right, i.e. VINDICATED it. "Far-fetched ... refuted" fails because a refuted theory would not be in every textbook; no one dismisses a theory as plausible.

stem: The witness's statement was deliberately ______: every sentence could be read in two ways, so neither lawyer could use it against her.
explanation: The colon introduces a definition: words that can be read in two ways are EQUIVOCAL (deliberately ambiguous). CANDID means frank and open, and EMPHATIC means forceful; a frank or forceful statement could easily be used against her.

stem: Hamza was ______ to hear that he had passed the exam, because he had been sure he had failed.
explanation: Good news he did not expect would make him DELIGHTED. BORED, ANNOYED and ASHAMED are reactions that do not fit hearing that a feared failure was actually a pass.

stem: The medicine is ______ only if taken on an empty stomach; with food, it has almost no effect.
explanation: The second half contrasts "almost no effect" with food, so on an empty stomach the medicine works: it is EFFECTIVE. USELESS is the trap; it describes what happens with food, not on an empty stomach.

stem: Ayesha is usually ______ in group discussions, so her classmates were ______ when she spoke for twenty minutes without stopping.
explanation: Speaking for twenty minutes must be unusual for her, so she is normally RETICENT (reluctant to speak) and her classmates were ASTONISHED. If she were talkative, no one would be astonished; "reticent ... unsurprised" breaks the cause-effect link signalled by "so".

stem: The old fort was in ______ condition: its walls had collapsed and its roof was gone.
explanation: The colon explains the condition: collapsed walls and no roof mean the fort was in RUINOUS condition. EXCELLENT and PERFECT say the opposite, and MODERN does not describe damage at all.

stem: Despite his ______ income, Usman managed to save enough money to pay for his sister's university fees.
explanation: "Despite" needs something that makes saving hard, so his income was MEAGRE (very small). GENEROUS, ENORMOUS and STEADY incomes would all make saving easier, so they remove the contrast.

stem: The committee's decision was ______: all twelve members voted in favour.
explanation: The colon gives the definition: when all members agree, the decision is UNANIMOUS. DIVIDED and CONTROVERSIAL describe disagreement, which "all twelve" rules out.

stem: Zainab's argument was so ______ that even her strongest opponents found it hard to ______ it.
explanation: "Even her strongest opponents" shows the argument was persuasive: COGENT (clear and convincing), so they could not REBUT (disprove) it. A feeble argument is easy to rebut, and "cogent ... accept" is illogical because a convincing argument is easy to accept.

stem: The library is a ______ place; talking loudly is not allowed.
explanation: A rule against loud talking keeps the library QUIET. NOISY is the opposite of what the rule produces, and COLOURFUL and DANGEROUS have nothing to do with talking.

stem: Sana's essay was ______ from start to finish; not a single paragraph strayed from the topic.
explanation: The second clause restates the blank: never straying from the topic means the essay was FOCUSED. RAMBLING and DIGRESSIVE both describe writing that wanders off the topic, the opposite.

stem: The road was closed for repairs; ______, we had to take a longer route through the hills.
explanation: The closure is the cause and the longer route is the result, so a result connector is needed: CONSEQUENTLY. NEVERTHELESS and IN CONTRAST signal a contrast that is not there, and ALTHOUGH cannot join clauses after a semicolon like this.

stem: Far from being a ______ achievement, the discovery was the result of twenty years of patient, methodical research.
explanation: "Far from being" needs the opposite of twenty years of methodical work, i.e. something that happened by lucky chance: FORTUITOUS. LABORIOUS, GRADUAL and SYSTEMATIC all describe what the discovery actually was, so they destroy the contrast.

stem: The desert plant is remarkably ______: it can survive months without rain by ______ water in its thick leaves.
explanation: Surviving months without rain shows the plant is HARDY (tough), and thick leaves suggest it survives by STORING water. FRAGILE and DELICATE contradict survival, and wasting water would not help it last through a drought.

stem: The baby was ______ by the loud thunder and began to cry.
explanation: Loud thunder that makes a baby cry has FRIGHTENED it. COMFORTED and CALMED are the opposite effect, and an AMUSED baby would laugh, not cry.

stem: Unlike his ______ brother, who spends every rupee he earns, Ali saves most of his salary.
explanation: "Unlike" contrasts the brother with saver Ali, and "spends every rupee" defines him as EXTRAVAGANT. THRIFTY and FRUGAL describe Ali himself, which would remove the contrast; WEALTHY says nothing about spending.

stem: The professor's lecture was so ______ that only a handful of students could follow its dense arguments and specialised terms.
explanation: Dense arguments and specialised terms that few could follow make the lecture ABSTRUSE (hard to understand). LUCID is the trap: it means clear and easy to follow, the opposite of the result described.

stem: The shop was ______ during the sale, but by evening it was almost ______ because most customers had gone home.
explanation: "But" contrasts the sale with the evening, and "customers had gone home" means the shop was nearly EMPTY, so during the sale it was CROWDED. "Crowded ... full" has no contrast, and "quiet ... deserted" does not fit a busy sale.

stem: The new policy was intended to ______ pollution, yet factory emissions in Lahore have risen sharply since it was introduced.
explanation: "Yet" shows the result went against the aim, and emissions rose, so the aim was to CURB (limit) pollution. A policy meant to increase or encourage pollution would make the rise expected, not a contrast.

stem: Because the evidence against him was ______, the judge had no choice but to ______ the accused, who walked free that afternoon.
explanation: "Walked free" shows the judge had to ACQUIT (declare not guilty), and "had no choice" means the evidence was FLIMSY (weak). Overwhelming evidence would not force an acquittal, and "convict" or "sentence" contradicts walking free.

stem: The water in the mountain stream was so ______ that we could see the pebbles at the bottom.
explanation: Being able to see the pebbles at the bottom is the result of CLEAR water. MUDDY water would hide them, and depth or warmth does not make the bottom visible.

stem: Hina's ______ nature made her the ideal person to settle the quarrel; she always listened to both sides before saying anything.
explanation: Listening to both sides before speaking is the definition of being IMPARTIAL (fair, not taking sides). BIASED is the opposite, and IMPULSIVE people act without listening first.

stem: The once-______ village has become ______ since the factory closed: most families have moved to Karachi in search of work.
explanation: "Once" signals a change for the worse: families leaving means the village is now DESERTED, so before the closure it was THRIVING. The reversed pair and "thriving ... prosperous" ignore the families moving away.

stem: The instructions were so ______ that nobody in the class understood what the assignment required.
explanation: Nobody understanding the task is the result of AMBIGUOUS (unclear, open to more than one meaning) instructions. EXPLICIT and PRECISE describe clear instructions, which would have the opposite result.

stem: Although Kamran is very ______, he never boasts about his wealth.
explanation: "His wealth" shows he is RICH, and "although" contrasts being rich with never boasting. HUMBLE and MODEST fit not boasting, so they leave no contrast for "although"; POOR contradicts his wealth.

stem: Her praise was so ______ that it seemed less like a compliment and more like an attempt to win the manager's favour.
explanation: Praise that is really an attempt to win favour is OBSEQUIOUS (too eager to please). SINCERE is the trap: sincere praise would be a genuine compliment, which the sentence denies; GRUDGING and RESTRAINED praise would be too cool to win favour.

stem: ______ it rained heavily all morning, the cricket match started on time because the pitch had been covered.
explanation: Heavy rain would normally delay a match, yet it started on time, so a contrast connector is needed: ALTHOUGH. BECAUSE and SINCE wrongly make the rain the reason the match started on time; UNLESS sets up a condition that makes no sense here.

stem: The first draft of the report contained many ______, so the editor ______ it before sending it to the printer.
explanation: "So" signals cause and effect: a draft with INACCURACIES (errors) would be FIXED before printing. Ignoring the errors is not a sensible result of finding them, and rejecting a draft for its insights is illogical.

stem: Zara was so ______ after the long journey that she fell asleep as soon as she sat down.
explanation: Falling asleep at once after a long journey shows she was WEARY (very tired). ENERGETIC, ALERT and LIVELY all describe someone wide awake.

stem: Lahore's old city is famous for its ______ streets, so narrow and winding that visitors often get lost.
explanation: Narrow, winding streets in which visitors get lost are LABYRINTHINE, like a maze. BROAD and STRAIGHT contradict "narrow and winding", and DESERTED says nothing about getting lost.

stem: The two reports were ______: one said the dam was safe, while the other warned that it could collapse.
explanation: One report says safe and the other says it could collapse, so they are CONTRADICTORY. IDENTICAL and CONSISTENT mean they agree, which the colon clause rules out.

stem: Ahmed studied ______ for the test, so he was ______ when he saw his excellent result.
explanation: "So" links cause and effect: studying HARD led to an excellent result, and an excellent result would leave him PLEASED. Studying little does not explain an excellent result, and being upset does not fit good news.

stem: The young author's first novel was praised for its ______ prose: not one word, critics noted, could be removed without loss.
explanation: If no word can be cut without loss, the writing uses no more words than needed: it is ECONOMICAL. FLORID, VERBOSE and ORNATE all describe wordy or over-decorated prose with plenty that could be removed.

stem: Many species of frog are now ______ because their wetland habitats have been drained for farming.
explanation: Losing their habitat is a cause of decline, so the frogs are ENDANGERED. ABUNDANT, THRIVING and MULTIPLYING describe growing populations, which draining their wetlands would not cause.

stem: Instead of ______ the problem, the manager chose to ______ it, hoping that it would somehow disappear on its own.
explanation: Hoping a problem will disappear on its own means choosing to IGNORE it, and "instead of" sets this against ADDRESSING (dealing with) it. The reversed pair contradicts the hope, and "solving ... fix" has no contrast.

stem: Though the medicine is ______ in small doses, it becomes ______ if a patient takes more than the prescribed amount.
explanation: "Though" demands a contrast between small doses and an overdose: BENEFICIAL in small amounts but TOXIC (poisonous) in large ones. "Harmful ... deadly" and "useless ... ineffective" are two words in the same direction, so there is no contrast.

stem: The teacher ______ the students for their hard work and gave them a day off.
explanation: Hard work and a reward (a day off) go with PRAISED. SCOLDED, PUNISHED and BLAMED are negative responses that do not match a reward.

stem: The museum guide spoke in such a ______ voice that the visitors at the back of the group could hardly hear her.
explanation: Visitors hardly hearing her is the result of a FAINT (weak, quiet) voice. BOOMING is the opposite, a very loud voice that everyone would hear.

stem: Rather than ______ the rumour, the company's long silence only seemed to confirm it.
explanation: "Rather than" contrasts the blank with "confirm", so the silence failed to DISPEL (drive away) the rumour. CONFIRM repeats the second half and leaves no contrast; spreading or inventing are not the opposite of confirming.

stem: Because Imran is ______, he spends hours checking every figure in his accounts before submitting them.
explanation: Spending hours checking every figure is the behaviour of a METICULOUS (extremely careful) person. NEGLIGENT, HASTY and INDIFFERENT all describe people who would not bother to check.

stem: The head teacher was known for her ______; she could deliver bad news so ______ that no one took offence.
explanation: No one taking offence shows she spoke GENTLY, which is what TACT (sensitivity in dealing with people) produces. Bluntness and rudeness would cause offence, and delivering news harshly contradicts the result.

stem: The data were too ______ to support a firm conclusion; the researchers recommended a larger study.
explanation: Recommending a larger study shows the problem was too little data, so the data were SCANTY. PLENTIFUL, RELIABLE and CONCLUSIVE data would support a firm conclusion, so "too ... to support" makes no sense with them.

stem: It was so ______ in Quetta that night that the water in the buckets turned to ice.
explanation: Water turns to ice only when it is very COLD. HOT and PLEASANT weather would not freeze water, and HUMID describes moisture in the air, not temperature.

stem: Far from ______ the plan, the new evidence actually ______ it, showing that the engineers' estimates had been correct all along.
explanation: Showing the estimates were correct means the evidence BOLSTERED (strengthened) the plan, and "far from" needs the opposite in the first blank: WEAKENING. "Supporting ... bolstered" has no contrast, and "weakening ... damaged" contradicts "far from".

stem: The explorer's account of the journey was ______; every distance, date and temperature he recorded has since been confirmed by satellite data.
explanation: Every figure being confirmed later shows the account was PRECISE (exact and accurate). EXAGGERATED and FANCIFUL accounts would be shown to be wrong, and VAGUE records would contain no exact figures to confirm.

stem: Initially ______ about the new technology, older farmers in Punjab became its most ______ supporters once they saw how much water drip irrigation saved.
explanation: "Initially" and "once they saw" mark a change of attitude: first WARY (cautious, doubtful), then ARDENT (passionate) supporters. "Eager ... ardent" shows no change, and "reluctant" or "hesitant" supporters does not fit being convinced by the water savings.

stem: The puppy was so ______ that it chewed through two shoes and a cushion in one afternoon.
explanation: Chewing shoes and a cushion is naughty behaviour, so the puppy was MISCHIEVOUS. An OBEDIENT, SLEEPY or GENTLE puppy would not cause that damage.

stem: The ______ of the medicine was clear within hours: the patient's fever dropped and he began to eat again.
explanation: The colon gives evidence that the medicine worked, and EFFICACY means the power to produce the intended effect. DANGER would show harmful effects, and COST and FLAVOUR are not shown by the fever dropping.

stem: The speaker's ______ remarks, made without any preparation, turned out to be the highlight of the conference.
explanation: "Made without any preparation" defines IMPROMPTU. REHEARSED is the opposite, and TEDIOUS remarks would not be the highlight of the conference.

stem: The bridge was built to be ______, but after the earthquake it proved surprisingly ______, with cracks appearing in every pillar.
explanation: "But" and "surprisingly" signal a contrast between the design and the result: built to be STURDY, it proved FRAGILE, as the cracks show. "Sturdy ... robust" has no contrast and contradicts the cracks; no bridge is built to be weak.

stem: Please speak ______; the baby has just fallen asleep.
explanation: A baby who has just fallen asleep should not be woken, so people should speak SOFTLY. LOUDLY is the opposite and would wake the baby; speed has nothing to do with it.

stem: Rather than ______ his mistake, Junaid tried to blame it on his teammates.
explanation: "Rather than" contrasts the blank with blaming others, so he failed to ACKNOWLEDGE (admit) his mistake. CONCEAL is the trap: blaming others is itself a way of concealing his fault, so there would be no contrast.

stem: The economist's forecast proved ______: within a year, every one of her predictions had come true.
explanation: Predictions that all came true show the forecast was PRESCIENT (showing knowledge of events before they happen). MISTAKEN is the opposite, and PREMATURE and HASTY suggest an unreliable forecast, which the colon clause contradicts.

stem: ______ the team trained hard all season, it lost the final; ______, the players were praised for their effort.
explanation: Training hard but losing is a contrast (ALTHOUGH), and being praised despite losing is a second contrast (EVEN SO). BECAUSE and SINCE wrongly make the training the cause of the defeat, and THEREFORE wrongly makes the defeat the reason for the praise.

stem: Ayaan was ______ when his best friend moved to another city, and he missed him every day.
explanation: Missing his friend every day shows he felt LONELY. JOYFUL and RELIEVED are positive feelings that do not fit losing a close friend's company, and PROUD has no link to the move.

stem: Solar panels are becoming more ______ in Pakistan as their price falls and electricity bills rise.
explanation: Cheaper panels and higher electricity bills are both reasons for more people to buy them, so they are becoming more POPULAR. EXPENSIVE contradicts the falling price, and RARE and OBSOLETE describe declining use.

stem: The ancient manuscript was so ______ that the historians had to handle it with gloves, turning each ______ page as gently as possible.
explanation: Handling it with gloves and turning pages gently show the manuscript was FRAGILE and its pages BRITTLE (easily broken). STURDY and DURABLE describe things that need no such care, and an ancient manuscript is not modern.

stem: The teacher's explanation was so ______ that even the weakest students understood the topic at once.
explanation: If even the weakest students understood at once, the explanation was LUCID (very clear). CONFUSING, OBSCURE and RUSHED explanations would leave weak students lost.

stem: The test was ______, so most students finished it ______ and left the hall early.
explanation: Leaving the hall early means the students finished QUICKLY, and "so" shows the cause: the test was EASY. A difficult or long test would not explain an early finish, and finishing slowly contradicts leaving early.

stem: The drought ______ the farmers' crops, leaving many families without an income.
explanation: Families left without an income show the crops were destroyed, so the drought DEVASTATED them. NOURISHED, IMPROVED and PROTECTED are positive effects, and a drought cannot leave people without income by helping crops.

stem: His ______ manner at the meeting, interrupting others and dismissing every suggestion, offended almost everyone present.
explanation: Interrupting and dismissing others is OVERBEARING (domineering) behaviour. DIFFIDENT and RESERVED describe shy, quiet people who would not interrupt, and COURTEOUS behaviour would not offend.

stem: Although the film had a ______ budget, it became a ______ success, earning ten times what it had cost.
explanation: Earning ten times its cost is a HUGE success, and "although" requires a contrast, so the budget was MODEST. "Modest ... minor" ignores the tenfold earnings, and "large ... huge" has no contrast.

stem: The cake tasted ______ because Sana had added salt instead of sugar.
explanation: Using salt instead of sugar would make a cake taste AWFUL. SWEET is the trap: without sugar the cake could not be sweet, and DELICIOUS and PERFECT contradict the mistake.

stem: The bus service is so ______ that it is impossible to plan a journey around it; sometimes it comes early, sometimes not at all.
explanation: Arriving early on some days and not at all on others is ERRATIC (unpredictable) behaviour. RELIABLE and PUNCTUAL say the opposite, and FREQUENT service would make planning easier, not impossible.

stem: The professor was ______ in her praise but ______ in her criticism, so students valued her rare compliments far more than her frequent comments on their mistakes.
explanation: "Rare compliments" means she was SPARING (giving little) with praise, and "frequent comments on their mistakes" means she was LIBERAL (giving freely) with criticism. "Lavish ... sparing" reverses the two, and "sparing ... restrained" ignores the frequent criticism.

stem: Bilal's apology seemed ______, since he repeated the same rude joke only minutes later.
explanation: Repeating the rude joke right after apologising shows he did not mean the apology, so it seemed INSINCERE. HEARTFELT and GENUINE are the opposite, which his behaviour rules out.

stem: The road through the hills is ______, so drivers must slow down at every bend.
explanation: A road with a bend after bend is WINDING. STRAIGHT is the opposite, and a WIDE or NEW road would not by itself force drivers to slow at every bend.

stem: Many young people in the village are ______ to leave their families, but they move to the city because there are no jobs at home.
explanation: "But" contrasts their feeling with the fact that they move anyway, so they are RELUCTANT (unwilling) to leave. EAGER, DELIGHTED and IMPATIENT would mean they want to go, leaving nothing for "but" to contrast.

stem: The ban on fishing in the lake was meant to be ______, lasting only until fish numbers recovered, but it remained in force for ten years.
explanation: "Lasting only until fish numbers recovered" defines TEMPORARY, and "but" contrasts this with the ten years. PERMANENT would leave no contrast with its long duration, and STRICT and POPULAR say nothing about time.

stem: Copper is widely used in electrical wiring because it is a good ______ of electricity and is also ______ enough to be drawn into thin wires.
explanation: Wiring must carry current, so copper is a good CONDUCTOR, and being drawn into thin wires is the definition of DUCTILE. An insulator blocks current, and a brittle metal would snap rather than stretch into wire.

stem: The scientist ______ the experiment three times to make sure the result was correct.
explanation: Doing the experiment three times to check the result means she REPEATED it. ABANDONED, FORGOT and AVOIDED all mean she did not do it, which cannot confirm a result.

stem: The company's annual report was full of ______ terms that few ordinary shareholders could understand.
explanation: Terms that few ordinary readers understand are ARCANE (known only to specialists). PLAIN, FAMILIAR and EVERYDAY words are easy for anyone, the opposite of the clue.

stem: The young chess player's victory was no ______; she had beaten three grandmasters in a row, proving her success was anything but ______.
explanation: Beating three grandmasters in a row shows skill, not luck: the win was no FLUKE (lucky chance) and anything but ACCIDENTAL. "Fluke ... deliberate" would deny that her success was deliberate, and "no triumph" contradicts beating grandmasters.

stem: The heavy rain made the mountain path so ______ that several hikers slipped and fell.
explanation: Rain and hikers slipping both point to a SLIPPERY path. DRY, FIRM and DUSTY are the opposite of a rain-soaked path and would not cause people to slip.

stem: Water ______ when it is heated to 100 °C at sea level.
explanation: At sea level water BOILS at 100 °C. It freezes at 0 °C, and condensing (gas to liquid) happens on cooling, not heating; ice melts, liquid water does not.

stem: Although the theory is elegant, it remains ______ because no experiment has yet been designed that could test it.
explanation: A theory that cannot yet be tested is SPECULATIVE (based on reasoning, not evidence). PROVEN and ESTABLISHED need experimental support, which the sentence says is missing, and OBSOLETE means replaced, which nothing suggests.

stem: Bees are ______ to farming: by ______ flowers, they help many fruit crops to grow.
explanation: Helping fruit crops grow makes bees VITAL (essential), and they do it by POLLINATING flowers. HARMFUL and IRRELEVANT contradict their help, and destroying flowers would not help crops grow.

stem: The new manager's policies were so ______ that, within a month, she had reversed almost every decision of her predecessor.
explanation: Reversing almost every earlier decision within a month is a RADICAL (far-reaching) change. CAUTIOUS, CONSERVATIVE and MODEST policies would change little, the opposite of the clue.

stem: Ali was ______ because he had lost his keys, but he became ______ when he found them in his pocket.
explanation: Losing keys makes a person WORRIED, and "but" marks the change when he found them: he became RELIEVED. The reversed pair puts the feelings in the wrong order, and "worried ... anxious" shows no change.

stem: Her ______ for languages was evident early: by the age of ten, she spoke Urdu, Pashto, English and Arabic fluently.
explanation: Speaking four languages fluently by ten shows a natural APTITUDE (talent) for them. AVERSION, INDIFFERENCE and CONTEMPT describe dislike or lack of interest, which her fluency contradicts.

stem: Usman's ______ was legendary: he would walk across the city rather than spend a few rupees on a rickshaw.
explanation: Refusing to spend even a few rupees is extreme reluctance to spend money, which is PARSIMONY. GENEROSITY and EXTRAVAGANCE describe free spending, the opposite, and an impatient person would hardly choose a long walk.

stem: Far from being ______, the new rules were so ______ that even small mistakes led to heavy fines.
explanation: Heavy fines for small mistakes mean the rules were STRINGENT (very strict), and "far from being" needs the opposite first: LENIENT. "Strict ... harsh" makes the sentence contradict itself, and the reversed pair does not fit the heavy fines.

stem: The bakery's bread never goes ______ on the shelves, because everything baked in the morning is sold out by noon.
explanation: Bread that is sold within hours has no time to go STALE (old and dry). The clue is the cause "sold out by noon"; bread does not go sweet or warm by sitting on a shelf.

stem: Rafay's ______ attitude to his studies worried his parents; he rarely opened a book and never did his homework.
explanation: Rarely opening a book and skipping homework shows a LACKADAISICAL (lazy, lacking effort) attitude. DILIGENT, EARNEST and STUDIOUS all describe a hard-working student, the opposite of what the semicolon clause describes.

stem: The factory installed new filters; ______, the air in the neighbourhood is much cleaner than it was last year.
explanation: The filters cause the cleaner air, so a result connector is needed: AS A RESULT. HOWEVER and EVEN SO signal a contrast, and OTHERWISE means "if not", which makes no sense here.

stem: The museum's collection is ______: it includes everything from ancient coins to modern paintings, ______ visitors of every interest.
explanation: Everything from ancient coins to modern paintings is a DIVERSE (varied) collection, and such variety would be ATTRACTING visitors of every interest. NARROW and LIMITED contradict the range described, and a varied collection would not repel visitors.

stem: The lazy cat spent the whole day ______ in the sun.
explanation: "Lazy" and lying in the sun all day fit DOZING (sleeping lightly). RUNNING, HUNTING and FIGHTING are active, which a lazy cat would not be doing all day.

stem: The diary offers a rare, ______ glimpse into village life in the 1940s, written by someone who lived through it rather than by a later historian.
explanation: Written by someone who lived through it means the account is FIRSTHAND. SECONDHAND describes exactly what the sentence excludes, a later historian's account, and FICTIONAL contradicts a real diary.

stem: The engineers had to ______ the launch of the satellite when a fault was found in its fuel system.
explanation: Finding a fault is a reason to delay, so they had to POSTPONE the launch. HASTEN (speed up) is the opposite, and celebrating a launch makes no sense when a fault has been found.

stem: The referee's decision, which was meant to ______ the angry players, only ______ them further, and the argument grew louder.
explanation: "Only" and "the argument grew louder" show the decision had the opposite effect from its aim: meant to CALM the players, it PROVOKED them. "Calm ... soothed" has no contrast and contradicts the louder argument; no referee aims to provoke players.

stem: Scientists have long sought to ______ the mystery of why some birds migrate thousands of kilometres each year.
explanation: Scientists seek to explain mysteries, so they want to UNRAVEL (solve) it. DEEPEN and CREATE would make the mystery bigger, and IGNORE contradicts "long sought".

stem: The candidate's answers were so ______ that, after an hour of questions, the interviewers still did not know what he actually thought.
explanation: If an hour of questions revealed nothing of his views, his answers were EVASIVE (avoiding giving a clear answer). CANDID, DIRECT and FORTHRIGHT all mean open and honest, which would have made his views clear.

stem: The room was so ______ that we had to switch on the lights, even though it was ______ outside at midday.
explanation: Switching on the lights means the room was DARK, and "even though" contrasts this with SUNNY weather outside. A bright room would not need lights, and it cannot be night at midday.

stem: The scientist's ______ approach, testing each idea carefully before moving on, meant her progress was slow but her results were trustworthy.
explanation: Testing each idea carefully before moving on is the definition of a METHODICAL (orderly, systematic) approach. HAPHAZARD, IMPULSIVE and CARELESS approaches would not produce trustworthy results.

stem: The old man was ______ but ______: although he had little money, he always shared his food with his neighbours.
explanation: The colon explains both blanks: "little money" means POOR, and sharing his food means GENEROUS, with "but" contrasting the two. "Rich" contradicts his little money, and "selfish" contradicts the sharing.

stem: After the long winter, the trees in the garden were ______ again, covered in bright green leaves.
explanation: Trees "covered in bright green leaves" are LEAFY. BARE and LEAFLESS describe the trees during winter, and "again" plus the leaves shows that stage is over.

stem: The author's tone is ______ throughout; she ______ the hardships of her childhood without self-pity, as if describing someone else.
explanation: Writing "as if describing someone else" is a DETACHED (emotionally distant) tone, and telling of hardships without self-pity means she simply RECOUNTS (narrates) them. LAMENTS means expresses grief, which clashes with "without self-pity"; a bitter tone is not emotionally distant.

stem: The ______ of the new road network is obvious: journeys that once took three hours now take less than one.
explanation: Shorter journeys are an advantage, so the colon clause shows the BENEFIT of the roads. DANGER and FAILURE are negative, and COST is not shown by journey times.

stem: Once a ______ figure who avoided crowds and rarely gave interviews, the singer now appears on television almost every week.
explanation: Avoiding crowds and rarely giving interviews defines a RECLUSIVE person, and "once ... now" contrasts this with appearing on television weekly. GREGARIOUS (sociable) is the opposite of the description given.

stem: The athlete's injury was more ______ than doctors had first thought, and she had to ______ from the competition.
explanation: An injury worse than expected forces an athlete out, so it was more SERIOUS and she had to WITHDRAW. A more minor injury would not force her out, and a serious injury would not help her advance.

stem: The children were ______ to see snow for the first time, and they ran outside shouting with joy.
explanation: Running outside "shouting with joy" shows the children were THRILLED. BORED, FRIGHTENED and UPSET contradict their joy.

stem: The lawyer's argument was ______: it seemed convincing at first, but it collapsed under careful examination.
explanation: An argument that seems convincing but fails when examined is SPECIOUS (plausible on the surface but wrong). SOUND, VALID and IRREFUTABLE describe arguments that would survive careful examination.

stem: The scientist's ______ attitude towards the results, refusing to accept them until they had been ______ by other laboratories, annoyed her impatient colleagues.
explanation: Refusing to accept results until others confirm them is CAUTIOUS, and other laboratories confirm results by repeating, i.e. REPLICATING, the work. A careless scientist would accept them at once, and waiting for others to ignore the results makes no sense.

stem: Because the shop was ______ on Friday, we had to come back on Saturday to buy the books.
explanation: Having to come back another day means they could not buy the books on Friday, so the shop was CLOSED. An open shop would have let them buy the books at once.

stem: The museum's collection of ancient pottery is ______; no other museum in the world has as many pieces from the Indus Valley.
explanation: If no other museum has as many pieces, the collection has no equal: it is UNRIVALLED. ORDINARY and MODEST suggest an average collection, which contradicts the second clause.

stem: Although the instructions looked ______ at first, they turned out to be quite ______ once the teacher explained them.
explanation: "Although" and "turned out" signal a change: the instructions looked COMPLICATED but were SIMPLE once explained. "Simple ... easy" and "clear ... obvious" show no change, and an explanation would not make them confusing.

stem: The film's ending was so ______ that audiences left the cinema arguing about what had actually happened; some found this ______, while others thought it was simply confusing.
explanation: Arguing about what happened shows the ending was CRYPTIC (mysterious), and "while" contrasts the second blank with "simply confusing", so it must be positive: FASCINATING. "Cryptic ... tedious" gives two negative reactions and no contrast; a predictable or obvious ending would not cause arguments.

stem: Hamza is very ______; he always helps his classmates with their homework.
explanation: Always helping classmates is the behaviour of a KIND person, as the semicolon clause explains. RUDE, SELFISH and LAZY people would not keep helping others.

stem: Pakistan's mountain glaciers are ______ rapidly as global temperatures rise, raising fears of floods and later water shortages.
explanation: Rising temperatures turn ice into water, so the glaciers are MELTING, which explains the fear of floods. GROWING, FREEZING and THICKENING would happen in colder conditions, not warmer ones.

stem: The new evidence ______ the old theory so completely that no serious scientist defends it today.
explanation: If no serious scientist defends the theory now, the evidence DISCREDITED it (showed it to be false). CONFIRMED, SUPPORTED and REVIVED would make scientists more likely to defend it.

stem: The village's water supply is ______ in summer, so residents must ______ every drop they use.
explanation: Having to take care with every drop shows water is SCARCE, so residents must CONSERVE (save) it. Plentiful water would not force anyone to save it, and wasting it is the opposite of the care described.

stem: Despite their ______ beginnings in a small rented room, the two engineers built one of the country's largest software companies.
explanation: A small rented room is a modest start, i.e. HUMBLE beginnings, and "despite" contrasts this with the huge company. GRAND, LAVISH and PRIVILEGED contradict the small rented room.

stem: The critic called the play ______, arguing that its plot was ______ and its characters had been seen a hundred times before.
explanation: Characters "seen a hundred times before" make the play HACKNEYED (overused, unoriginal), and its plot fits that criticism: PREDICTABLE. "Hackneyed ... innovative" contradicts itself, and ORIGINAL and FRESH are praise, not the criticism described.

stem: The soup was too ______ to eat, so Ayesha waited for it to ______ down.
explanation: Waiting for soup to become eatable means it was too HOT and needed to COOL down. Cold soup would not need cooling, and waiting does not make salty soup less salty.

stem: The prize is awarded only to students whose work is truly ______; ordinary or copied projects are never considered.
explanation: The second clause excludes ordinary and copied work, so the prize needs ORIGINAL work. BORROWED means copied and AVERAGE and ROUTINE mean ordinary, exactly the kinds of work ruled out.

stem: Her ______ remarks about her colleague's work, always polite on the surface but quietly mocking, made the atmosphere in the office tense.
explanation: Polite on the surface but quietly mocking describes BARBED remarks (with a hidden, hurtful edge). SINCERE, FLATTERING and ENCOURAGING remarks would not mock anyone or make the office tense.

stem: The patient's condition was ______ at first, but after a week of treatment it ______ steadily and he was sent home.
explanation: Being sent home shows his condition IMPROVED, and "but" requires a bad start: CRITICAL. "Critical ... deteriorated" contradicts being sent home, and "excellent ... improved" has no contrast.

stem: Bilal felt ______ after eating three plates of biryani.
explanation: After eating three plates a person feels FULL. HUNGRY, EMPTY and STARVING describe how someone feels before eating, not after a large meal.

stem: Because the bridge was ______, the engineers ______ it to traffic until repairs were completed.
explanation: "Until repairs were completed" shows the bridge was CLOSED, and the cause ("because") must be that it was UNSAFE. A safe bridge would not be closed for repairs, and opening an unsafe bridge contradicts the repairs.

stem: Because the team's star player was ______, the coach had to ______ the line-up at the last minute.
explanation: A last-minute problem with the star player forces the coach to CHANGE the line-up, and "because" needs a reason such as being INJURED. A fit player gives no reason to change it, and keeping the line-up is not something a coach is forced to do at the last minute.

stem: The scientist's findings were ______ by three independent teams, so there is little doubt that they are correct.
explanation: "So there is little doubt" shows the other teams confirmed the findings: they CORROBORATED them. CONTRADICTED and QUESTIONED would create doubt, and IGNORED findings gain no support.

stem: Sana's ______ in the face of repeated failure finally paid off when her fifth business proposal was accepted.
explanation: Trying a fifth time after four failures shows TENACITY (determination to keep going). COMPLACENCY, TIMIDITY and APATHY would all make her give up, so they could not "pay off".

stem: The new teacher was ______ at first, but as the weeks passed she became more ______ and began to joke with her students.
explanation: Beginning to joke shows she became more RELAXED, and "but" with "at first" needs the opposite earlier: RESERVED. The reversed pair contradicts the joking, and the other pairs show no change.

stem: The ______ wind blew the roofs off several houses in the storm.
explanation: A wind strong enough to blow roofs off houses is FIERCE. GENTLE, MILD and LIGHT winds could not do such damage.

stem: The professor's ______ knowledge of history amazed her students: she could answer questions on any period, from the ancient world to the modern day.
explanation: Being able to answer on any period shows ENCYCLOPAEDIC (wide-ranging, complete) knowledge. SUPERFICIAL, LIMITED and PATCHY knowledge would leave gaps, which the colon clause rules out.

stem: Electric cars produce no exhaust fumes; ______, they are often promoted as a cleaner choice for crowded cities.
explanation: Producing no fumes is the reason they are called cleaner, so a cause-result connector is needed: FOR THIS REASON. HOWEVER, IN CONTRAST and NEVERTHELESS signal a contrast, but the two clauses agree.

stem: The scientist's early papers were largely ______, but her later work was so ______ that it changed the direction of the whole field.
explanation: Changing the direction of a field means the later work was INFLUENTIAL, and "but" needs a contrast, so the early papers were OVERLOOKED (not noticed). "Praised ... influential" has no contrast, and insignificant work could not change a whole field.

stem: The witness's story kept changing, which made the police ______ of her account.
explanation: A story that keeps changing causes doubt, so the police became SUSPICIOUS of it. CONVINCED and CERTAIN are the opposite of doubt, which the changing story would not produce.

stem: The bag was so ______ that Sana could not lift it, so her brother ______ it for her.
explanation: Not being able to lift the bag means it was HEAVY, and her brother helping means he CARRIED it for her. A light or empty bag would be easy to lift, and dropping it would not help her.

stem: The report's conclusions were ______ at best: they rested on a single small survey that the authors themselves admitted was flawed.
explanation: Conclusions resting on one small, flawed survey are TENUOUS (very weak), and "at best" signals a negative judgement. ROBUST, DEFINITIVE and COMPELLING describe strong conclusions, the opposite of what the colon clause shows.

stem: The noise from the construction site was so ______ that students in the nearby school could not concentrate.
explanation: Noise that stops students concentrating is DISRUPTIVE. FAINT and DISTANT noise would hardly be noticed, and PLEASANT noise would not prevent study.

stem: Hassan's ______ was well known; he could never keep a secret and ______ every piece of news to anyone who would listen.
explanation: Never keeping a secret is INDISCRETION, and telling every piece of news to anyone means he BROADCAST it. DISCRETION means keeping things private, the opposite, and "concealed" contradicts his inability to keep secrets.

stem: The farmer was ______ because the rain had finally come after months of dry weather.
explanation: Rain after months of dry weather is good news for crops, so the farmer was PLEASED. "Finally" shows he had been waiting for it, which rules out ANGRY and WORRIED.

stem: The architect's design was praised for its ______: the building used half the energy of similar offices.
explanation: Using half the energy of similar buildings shows EFFICIENCY. EXTRAVAGANCE and WASTEFULNESS mean using too much, the opposite, and HEIGHT has nothing to do with energy use.

stem: The explorer's supplies were nearly ______, so he had to ______ his food carefully for the rest of the journey.
explanation: Having to manage food carefully shows his supplies were nearly EXHAUSTED (used up), so he had to RATION (limit) what he ate. Plentiful supplies would not need rationing, and wasting food contradicts "carefully".

stem: Rather than being ______ by his defeat in the first round, the young boxer trained harder and won the title the following year.
explanation: "Rather than" contrasts the blank with training harder, so he refused to be DISCOURAGED. ENCOURAGED, INSPIRED and MOTIVATED all point the same way as training harder, leaving no contrast.

stem: The fabric is ______, allowing air to pass through it and keeping the wearer cool in the Karachi heat.
explanation: "Allowing air to pass through it" defines POROUS (full of tiny holes). AIRTIGHT and IMPERMEABLE mean nothing can pass through, the opposite, and a heavy fabric would not keep the wearer cool.

stem: Our neighbour's dog is very ______; it barks at everyone who walks past the gate.
explanation: Barking at everyone who passes makes the dog NOISY, as the semicolon clause explains. QUIET and SILENT are the opposite, and a sleepy dog would not bark at every passer-by.

stem: Though the professor's lectures were ______, packed with difficult ideas, her written notes were remarkably ______, so students relied on them to make sense of each class.
explanation: "Packed with difficult ideas" defines DENSE, and students relying on the notes to understand shows the notes were CLEAR; "though" confirms the contrast. Obscure notes would not help, and simple lectures contradict "difficult ideas".

stem: The tea was so ______ that Bilal added three more spoonfuls of sugar.
explanation: Adding a lot of sugar is a response to tea that tastes BITTER. SWEET and SUGARY tea would not need more sugar, and sugar does nothing to cool hot tea.

stem: The novel's ______ plot, with its dozens of characters and countless twists, demands a patient and attentive reader.
explanation: Dozens of characters and countless twists make a CONVOLUTED (complicated, hard to follow) plot. SIMPLE, STRAIGHTFORWARD and BRIEF plots would not demand a patient, attentive reader.

stem: Fatima ______ the job offer because the salary was too ______ to cover her rent in Islamabad.
explanation: A salary that cannot cover the rent is too LOW, and that is a reason to have DECLINED the offer. Accepting it because of a low salary is illogical, and a high salary would easily cover the rent.

stem: Exercise is ______ to good health, so doctors advise at least thirty minutes of walking each day.
explanation: Doctors advising daily walking shows exercise is ESSENTIAL (necessary) to good health. If it were HARMFUL or UNRELATED, doctors would have no reason to advise it.

stem: The negotiator's ______ approach, refusing to give up even a single point, made a compromise impossible.
explanation: Refusing to give up a single point is INTRANSIGENT (unwilling to change one's position). FLEXIBLE, CONCILIATORY and ACCOMMODATING all describe someone ready to compromise, the opposite of the clue.

stem: The once-______ river is now so ______ that fish can no longer survive in it.
explanation: Fish being unable to survive shows the river is now POLLUTED, and "once" marks a change from an earlier state: CLEAN. The reversed pair would let fish survive, and "dirty ... toxic" shows no change.

stem: Ayesha's ______ reply, just a single word, left her friends wondering whether she was upset.
explanation: A reply of a single word is TERSE (brief to the point of seeming rude), which is why her friends wondered if she was upset. LENGTHY and DETAILED contradict the single word, and a cheerful reply would not cause that worry.

stem: The scholar was famously ______: she would spend weeks checking a single ______ before allowing it into her book.
explanation: Spending weeks checking one small point shows she was FASTIDIOUS (extremely careful about accuracy), and the thing checked is a single DETAIL. SLAPDASH, CARELESS and HASTY describe the opposite kind of worker.

stem: Hamza's explanation was ______ with the facts: every detail he gave matched the security camera footage.
explanation: Every detail matching the footage means his explanation was CONSISTENT with the facts. INCONSISTENT is the trap: it means the details did not match, the opposite of the colon clause.

stem: The medicine relieved the pain ______, but the effect was only ______: within two hours the headache had returned.
explanation: A headache returning within two hours shows the effect was TEMPORARY, and "but ... only" contrasts this with a good start: the pain went QUICKLY. "Permanent" and "lasting" contradict the returning headache, and a medicine that never relieved pain had no effect to wear off.

stem: Critics found the speech ______, full of grand phrases but empty of any real ideas.
explanation: Grand-sounding language with little meaning is BOMBASTIC. SUBSTANTIVE and PROFOUND mean full of real ideas, which the sentence denies, and UNDERSTATED contradicts the grand phrases.

stem: The lake was so ______ that the children could stand up anywhere in it.
explanation: Standing up anywhere in a lake is possible only if the water is SHALLOW. DEEP is the opposite, and WIDE or COLD water says nothing about whether children can stand.

stem: Rather than ______ the old building, the city decided to ______ it and turn it into a public library.
explanation: Turning the building into a library means it was kept and RESTORED, and "rather than" needs the opposite in the first blank: DEMOLISH. The reversed pair leaves no building for a library, and "repair ... renovate" has no contrast.

stem: Because of the ______ weather, the fishing boats at Gwadar stayed in harbour for a week.
explanation: Boats staying in harbour for a week is the result of dangerous, STORMY weather. CALM, SUNNY and PLEASANT weather would allow them to go out to sea.

stem: The student gave ______ answers to the simplest questions, so the examiner was ______ that she had read the book at all.
explanation: "At all" signals doubt, so the examiner was DOUBTFUL, and "so" shows the cause: VAGUE answers to simple questions. Clear answers would not cause doubt, and vague answers would not make him convinced.

stem: The kitten was so ______ that it fitted in the palm of Zainab's hand.
explanation: Fitting in the palm of a hand means the kitten was TINY. HUGE and HEAVY are the opposite of the size described, and FIERCE says nothing about size.

stem: Sana wanted to go to the park, ______ it was raining, so she stayed at home.
explanation: Wanting to go out and the rain that stopped her are in contrast, so BUT is needed. BECAUSE would make the rain her reason for wanting to go, and UNLESS sets up a condition that does not fit the past events.

stem: The museum guide was ______ about the paintings; she could answer every question the visitors ______.
explanation: Answering every question shows she was KNOWLEDGEABLE, and the questions she answered were the ones the visitors ASKED. An ignorant or confused guide could not answer every question, and visitors do not ignore their own questions.

stem: Despite the ______ forecast, the day turned out bright and sunny.
explanation: "Despite" needs a forecast that went against the bright, sunny day, so it was GLOOMY (predicting dull or bad weather). CHEERFUL, OPTIMISTIC and SUNNY forecasts would agree with the weather, leaving no contrast.

stem: Zubair is ______ about his work; he never leaves a task half-finished.
explanation: Never leaving a task half-finished shows he is CONSCIENTIOUS (careful to do his work well and fully). CARELESS and CASUAL describe the opposite attitude, and a RELUCTANT worker would be likely to leave tasks unfinished.

stem: The road was ______ after the storm, so the bus arrived ______.
explanation: "So" links cause and effect: a BLOCKED road would make the bus LATE. A clear road would not cause lateness, and a blocked road would not make it early.

stem: The scientist's ______ claims, made without evidence and repeated in every interview, damaged her reputation among her colleagues.
explanation: Claims "made without evidence" are UNFOUNDED. VERIFIED claims have been checked and confirmed, the opposite, and MODEST or CAUTIOUS claims would not damage a scientist's reputation.

stem: The ______ of the medicine is unpleasant, so it is coated with sugar to make it easier to swallow.
explanation: A sugar coating hides a bad TASTE. It does not change the size, colour or price of the medicine, so those words do not explain the sugar coating.

stem: Although she had been ______ in her youth, spending every rupee as soon as she earned it, in old age she became remarkably ______.
explanation: Spending every rupee at once defines PROFLIGATE (recklessly wasteful), and "although" needs the opposite in old age: FRUGAL (careful with money). The reversed pair contradicts her youthful spending, and "profligate ... wasteful" has no contrast.

stem: The two sisters look so ______ that even their teachers cannot tell them apart.
explanation: Not being able to tell two people apart means they look ALIKE. DIFFERENT and UNLIKE are the opposite, and being TALL would not make them hard to tell apart.

stem: The team's victory was ______; they had not lost a single match all season, so everyone expected them to win.
explanation: "Everyone expected them to win" makes the victory PREDICTABLE. SHOCKING and UNEXPECTED contradict that expectation, and a team unbeaten all season did not win by luck.

stem: Many people find mathematics ______, but with regular practice it becomes far less ______.
explanation: "But" and "far less" show practice reduces the problem, so mathematics seems DIFFICULT and becomes less CHALLENGING. Practice would not make it less manageable or less interesting, and if it were easy there would be nothing to reduce.

stem: The patient was too ______ to walk, so the nurse brought a wheelchair.
explanation: Needing a wheelchair shows the patient was too WEAK to walk. STRONG, HEALTHY and FIT people can walk, so "too ... to walk" makes no sense with them.

stem: His ______ refusal to listen to advice led to one costly mistake after another.
explanation: A stubborn refusal to listen is OBSTINATE. OPEN-MINDED, FLEXIBLE and RECEPTIVE all describe someone willing to listen, which contradicts "refusal to listen".

stem: Hamza practised every day; ______, he still found the final piece difficult to play.
explanation: Daily practice should make the piece easy, yet it was still difficult, so a contrast connector is needed: EVEN SO. THEREFORE and AS A RESULT wrongly make the practice the cause of the difficulty, and BECAUSE cannot follow the semicolon this way.

stem: The ______ child shared her sweets with everyone in the class.
explanation: Sharing sweets with everyone is GENEROUS behaviour. GREEDY, SELFISH and MEAN children would keep the sweets for themselves.

stem: The report was ______ by the committee for being too ______; members complained that it took an hour to read yet said almost nothing.
explanation: Members complaining shows the report was FAULTED (criticised), and taking an hour to say almost nothing means it was too WORDY. Committees do not praise or welcome a report they complain about, and a concise report would not take an hour to read.

stem: The ______ sound of the waves helped Fatima fall asleep.
explanation: A sound that helps someone fall asleep is SOOTHING (calming). JARRING, DEAFENING and ALARMING sounds would keep her awake.

stem: The young violinist's performance was so ______ that the audience rose to its feet before the final note had faded.
explanation: An audience rising to its feet at once shows the performance was CAPTIVATING (holding everyone's attention). MEDIOCRE, LACKLUSTRE and TEDIOUS performances would not bring a crowd to its feet.

stem: Because the hall was ______, many latecomers had to ______ at the back.
explanation: Latecomers standing at the back shows there were no free seats, so the hall was PACKED and they had to STAND. In an empty hall they could simply sit down, and leaving "at the back" makes no sense.

stem: Junaid's ______ remark, made without thinking, hurt his friend's feelings.
explanation: "Made without thinking" defines a THOUGHTLESS remark, and such remarks often hurt people. CONSIDERATE, TACTFUL and CAREFUL remarks are made with thought for others.

stem: The ______ of the mountain village made it hard for doctors to reach during winter.
explanation: A place that is hard to reach is far from towns and roads, so its REMOTENESS is the cause. BEAUTY, SIZE and FAME do not make a village hard to reach.

stem: Initially ______ to the idea of moving abroad, Usman gradually became ______ to it after visiting the university in person.
explanation: "Initially" and "gradually became" show a change: first HOSTILE (opposed) to the idea, then RECONCILED (accepting) after the visit. "Hostile ... opposed" shows no change, and "receptive ... reconciled" gives him nothing to come to terms with.

stem: The laptop's battery is so ______ that it lasts only an hour on a full charge.
explanation: Lasting only an hour shows the battery is WEAK. POWERFUL, DURABLE and EFFICIENT batteries would last much longer, the opposite of "only an hour".

stem: The scientist was ______ about her findings, refusing to claim more than her data could show.
explanation: Refusing to claim more than the data show is CIRCUMSPECT (cautious, careful not to take risks). BOASTFUL, RECKLESS and EXTRAVAGANT describe someone who would overstate the findings.

stem: The once-quiet market is now so ______ that shopkeepers have had to hire extra staff to ______ the crowds.
explanation: "Once-quiet" and "crowds" show the market is now BUSY, and extra staff are hired to SERVE the customers. Hiring staff to ignore crowds makes no sense, and quiet or empty contradicts the crowds.

stem: The scientist's explanation was ______: in a few simple sentences, she made a difficult idea clear to everyone.
explanation: "A few simple sentences" that make an idea clear describe a SUCCINCT explanation (brief and clear). RAMBLING is long and wandering, and OBSCURE and CONVOLUTED explanations are hard to follow.

stem: Rather than ______ the dispute between the two neighbours, the council's ruling only ______ it, and they stopped speaking altogether.
explanation: The neighbours stopping speaking shows the ruling INFLAMED (worsened) the dispute, and "rather than" needs the opposite first: SETTLING it. The reversed pair contradicts the result, and "settling ... resolved" has no contrast.

stem: The hikers were ______ by the beauty of the valley and stopped for an hour just to look at it.
explanation: Stopping for an hour just to admire the view shows they were ENCHANTED (delighted). UNIMPRESSED, BORED and ANNOYED hikers would not stop to look for so long.

stem: ______ he was tired, Ahmed finished his homework before going to bed.
explanation: Being tired would make him want to skip the homework, yet he finished it, so a contrast is needed: EVEN THOUGH. BECAUSE wrongly makes tiredness the reason he finished, SO THAT expresses purpose, and UNLESS sets up a condition that does not fit.

stem: The scientist ______ her earlier results when new data showed that her first calculations had been ______.
explanation: New data showing the calculations were FLAWED (wrong) would lead her to have REVISED her results. Defending results shown to be wrong is illogical, and perfect calculations would need no revision.

stem: The author's ______ style, full of long sentences and rare words, makes her books hard going for younger readers.
explanation: Long sentences and rare words make a style ORNATE (elaborate, heavily decorated). PLAIN, SIMPLE and SPARSE styles use short, common words and would be easy for younger readers.

stem: The committee's ______ approval, given only after months of debate and with many conditions, disappointed those who had hoped for wholehearted support.
explanation: Approval given slowly and with many conditions, short of wholehearted support, is GRUDGING (given reluctantly). ENTHUSIASTIC, IMMEDIATE and UNCONDITIONAL are each contradicted by the months of debate and the many conditions.

stem: The weather in the north was ______, so the climbers ______ their attempt on the summit until the storms had passed.
explanation: Storms make mountain weather TREACHEROUS (dangerous), and waiting until they passed means the climbers DELAYED their attempt. Pleasant or mild weather would give no reason to wait, and hastening contradicts "until the storms had passed".

stem: Bilal's room is usually ______, with clothes and books everywhere, so his mother was ______ to find it tidy.
explanation: Clothes and books everywhere describe a MESSY room, so finding it tidy for once would leave his mother AMAZED. "Unsurprised" breaks the link signalled by "so", and a usually tidy room would not amaze her.
